source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with known panic disorder arrives saying, 'Help me, I think I'm having a heart attack.' What is the nurse's PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Panic disorder can cause chest pain and palpitations, but a physical cause must be ruled out first. The nurse assesses the physical condition before anything else.
explanations: Correct: rule out a physiological cause first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q56 (PDF p. 197)
questions.quote: The priority is to assess the client’s physical condition to rule out a physiological disorder for these signs and symptoms.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which belief does the nurse expect to find in a client with bulimia nervosa?
options: She overeats when she loses control
questions.rationale: Bulimia involves cycles of binge eating followed by purging, which the client views as acceptable. Binge eating without purging is seen in obesity.
explanations: Correct: purging is seen as acceptable.
More typical of an obese binge eater.
More typical of an obese binge eater.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q164 (PDF p. 315)
questions.quote: Individuals with bulimia nervosa develop cycles of binge eating, followed by purging.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Jasmine, 16, is admitted with anorexia nervosa. She is very thin and is constantly worried about gaining weight.
questions.stem: The nurse finds Jasmine doing vigorous push-ups in her room. What should the nurse do?
options: Stop her and weigh her now
Ignore it to avoid a power struggle
questions.rationale: Clients with anorexia often exercise rigorously to burn off calories. The nurse provides appropriate exercise and sets limits on excessive activity. Weighing her would reinforce her altered self-concept.
explanations: Correct: limit excess activity and offer appropriate exercise.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q167 (PDF p. 320)
questions.quote: The nurse must provide for appropriate exercise, as well as place limits on rigorous activities.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Jasmine, 16, is admitted with anorexia nervosa. She is very thin and is constantly worried about gaining weight.
questions.stem: Which statement by Jasmine is the PRIORITY for further assessment?
questions.rationale: Exercising 3 to 4 hours daily is excessive and unrealistic for a 16-year-old and needs immediate follow-up. Daily weighing is common in anorexia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q880 (PDF p. 1120)
questions.quote: Exercising 3 to 4 hours every day is excessive physical activity and unrealistic for a 16-year-old girl.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding supports a diagnosis of SEVERE depression?
questions.rationale: Severe depression typically brings weight loss and insomnia, a flat affect, and statements like 'I have no more tears.' Mild depression may bring weight gain and hypersomnia.
explanations: Severely depressed clients may have no tears left.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q309 (PDF p. 473)
questions.quote: In the severely depressed client, loss of weight is typical, whereas the mildly depressed client may experience a gain in weight.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Two days after admission for moderate depression, a client suddenly smiles and says the crisis is over. What should the nurse do?
options: Allow more time alone in room
questions.rationale: Such a quick 'cure' is unlikely. A sudden lift in mood may mean the client has decided on self-harm, so suicide precautions are needed.
explanations: Correct: a sudden mood lift may signal a suicide plan.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q414 (PDF p. 591)
questions.quote: When a mood suddenly lifts, it is likely that the client may have made the decision to cause self-harm.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: When should the nurse add extra precautions for a client with suicidal ideation?
questions.rationale: Fewer staff are available at shift change, so precautions increase then. Nights and weekends are also high-risk times.
explanations: Weekends, not weekdays, are higher risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q415 (PDF p. 592)
questions.quote: At shift change, there is often less availability of staff.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An older adult is identified as a victim of psychological abuse at home. What is the PRIORITY nursing action?
options: Call a social worker for the family
Remove her from the abusive setting
questions.rationale: The priority is to remove the victim from the abusive environment. Treatment, reporting, and case work also follow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q425 (PDF p. 602)
questions.quote: The priority nursing intervention is to remove the abused victim from the abusive environment.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client admitted with suicidal ideation is about to go home. Which family statement may justify delaying discharge?
options: 'Does he know I've moved out and filed for separation?'
'I postponed my wedding so he can attend.'
'We set up his room just like before.'
questions.rationale: Separated, divorced, and widowed people have higher suicide rates. Unknown news of a separation is a serious stressor for a client with suicidal ideation.
explanations: Correct: a major new loss raises suicide risk.
Can make him feel included and valued.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q591 (PDF p. 799)
questions.quote: Single, divorced, and widowed clients have suicide rates that are greater than those who are married.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with mania comes out of her room topless, making lewd gestures. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Quietly escort her to her room to dress
Give her a time-out as a consequence
questions.rationale: Mania impairs insight, judgment, and impulse control. The nurse takes control calmly without adding stress. Confrontation or insisting may cause resistance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q803 (PDF p. 1037)
questions.quote: The nurse must take control without creating increased stress or anxiety for the client.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: After witnessing a friend's murder, a client has trouble concentrating, angry outbursts, and feels 'keyed up.' What should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: PTSD follows a markedly distressing event. It causes sustained anxiety, sleep problems, irritability, poor concentration, and angry outbursts.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q820 (PDF p. 1054)
questions.quote: PTSD is a response to an event that would be markedly distressing to almost anyone.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which therapeutic action belongs in the care plan for an 11-year-old who was physically abused?
options: Have the child confront the abuser
Provide a setting that builds trust
Teach the child to avoid abuse
Tell the child it wasn't serious
questions.rationale: Abused children need long-term support in an environment that models trust and empathy, where healing can begin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q830 (PDF p. 1066)
questions.quote: The environment provided during the child’s healing must include one in which trust and empathy are modeled and provided for the child.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A 14-year-old with burns and bruises says, 'I'm afraid to go home; my stepfather will be angry I told.' What is the BEST response?
questions.rationale: An abused child is admitted for a full evaluation and protection. An empathic statement assures the child of safety and supports them as the victim.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q837 (PDF p. 1073)
questions.quote: A child who has been physically and sexually abused should be admitted to the hospital.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which question is MOST important when assessing a client's suicide risk?
options: 'Why do you want to hurt yourself?'
'Do you have a plan to hurt yourself?'
'Has anyone in your family died by suicide?'
questions.rationale: A client with a definite plan is at greater risk. 'Why' questions put the client on the defensive.
explanations: 'Why' puts the client on the defensive.
Correct: a plan indicates higher risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q845 (PDF p. 1082)
questions.quote: Clients who have a definitive plan pose a greater risk for suicide.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is an EXPECTED short-term side effect of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)?
questions.rationale: The main expected side effects of ECT are confusion, disorientation, and memory loss. Hypertension or palpitations are concerning and are reported.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q846 (PDF p. 1083)
questions.quote: The major expected side effects of ECT are confusion, disorientation, and memory loss.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Mang Danilo, 35, is admitted in the manic phase of bipolar disorder. He is restless, talks nonstop, and sleeps very little.
questions.stem: Which meal is BEST for Mang Danilo?
options: Beef stew with fruit salad and tea
Macaroni with a fork and coffee
questions.rationale: A client in mania is too active to sit through meals and often under-eats. Finger foods he can eat 'on the run' are best, and caffeine is avoided.
explanations: Needs utensils, and tea has caffeine.
Correct: high-calorie finger foods, no caffeine.
Needs utensils, and coffee has caffeine.
Needs utensils, and coffee has caffeine.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q853 (PDF p. 1090)
questions.quote: Foods that the client can eat “on the run” are best because the client is too active to sit at meals and use utensils.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Mang Danilo, 35, is admitted in the manic phase of bipolar disorder. He is restless, talks nonstop, and sleeps very little.
questions.stem: Mang Danilo starts organizing a dance for the whole unit at suppertime. What should the nurse encourage instead?
options: Asking other staff to help organize
A quiet, solitary activity like writing
questions.rationale: A manic client is easily stimulated by the environment, so quiet, solitary activities such as writing are the best outlet for his energy. A newly admitted client is likely to have impaired judgment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q857 (PDF p. 1094)
questions.quote: Because the client with bipolar disorder is easily stimulated by the environment, sedentary activities are the best outlets for energy release.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An abused child copes by using repression. Which activity should the nurse include in the plan?
options: Therapeutic play to act out experiences
Telling the child to forget the past
Avoiding any talk of the abuse
questions.rationale: Therapeutic play with art, dolls, or puppets is a nonthreatening way for a child to act out frightening experiences. The other options threaten the child or force further repression.
explanations: Correct: a safe outlet for trauma.
Devalues the child and forces repression.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q854 (PDF p. 1091)
questions.quote: It is a nonthreatening avenue through which the child can use artwork, dolls, or puppets to act out frightening life experiences.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An older client living with family arrives with poor hygiene, contractures, and multiple pressure ulcers. Which form of victimization is suspected?
questions.rationale: Physical abuse can be battering or the subtler neglect, a failure to meet basic needs. Poor hygiene, contractures, and pressure ulcers point to neglect.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q855 (PDF p. 1092)
questions.quote: or it can be more subtle, such as neglect (the failure to meet basic needs).

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia says, 'I am Elizabeth, the Queen of England.' What is this?
questions.rationale: A delusion is a firmly held false belief that resists change; claiming to be royalty is grandiose. An illusion misreads real stimuli, and a hallucination is a false perception.
explanations: Ideas that shift between unrelated subjects.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q856 (PDF p. 1093)
questions.quote: A delusion is an important personal belief that is almost certainly not true and that resists modification.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why should the nurse initially allow a client with OCD to continue hand-washing rituals?
options: It lowers the risk of infection
questions.rationale: The compulsive act gives immediate relief from anxiety and is used to cope with stress. Stopping it abruptly would increase anxiety.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q858 (PDF p. 1095)
questions.quote: The compulsive act provides immediate relief from anxiety and is used to cope with stress, conflict, or pain.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An anxious client is blocking the hallway, taking three steps forward and two back. How should the nurse intervene?
options: Stand beside the client: 'You're very anxious today.'
Tell the client: 'You're going to have to stop that.'
Tell other clients to walk around
Distract the client with a TV show
questions.rationale: To ease anxiety, the nurse helps the client recognize the behavior. Demands or ignoring the behavior may escalate it.
explanations: Correct: helps the client recognize the anxiety.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q861 (PDF p. 1098)
questions.quote: An important consideration when alleviating anxiety is to assist the client with recognizing the behavior.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In which therapy does the client act out situations of emotional significance?
questions.rationale: Psychodrama involves acting out emotionally charged situations. Psychoanalytic and short-term dynamic therapies draw on psychoanalytic techniques.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q862 (PDF p. 1099)
questions.quote: Psychodrama involves the enactment of emotionally charged situations.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A manic client who assaulted another client is to be secluded. What should the nurse do BEFORE seclusion?
options: Stay silent to avoid more agitation
Tell her directly why she is being secluded
questions.rationale: Seclusion removes the client to a nonstimulating room for protection and close supervision. The nurse informs the client directly of its purpose; it is never framed as punishment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q863 (PDF p. 1100)
questions.quote: It is best to directly inform the client of the purpose of the seclusion.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with catatonic schizophrenia lies curled in a fetal position. Which approach BEST builds communication?
options: Leave the client alone all day
Sit in silence; ask open questions
Insist the client join group therapy
questions.rationale: Withdrawn clients need consistent, repeated contact. Sitting in silence, asking open-ended questions, and pausing for responses build communication.
explanations: Direct questions are not effective here.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q865 (PDF p. 1102)
questions.quote: The nurse facilitates communication with the client by sitting in silence, asking open-ended questions, and pausing to provide opportunities for the client to respond.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: After a gastrostomy tube is placed, a client refuses care, avoids eye contact, and will not talk. Which coping mechanism is this?
questions.rationale: Distancing is an unwillingness or inability to discuss events, shown here by withdrawal and refusal to engage.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q870 (PDF p. 1107)
questions.quote: Distancing is an unwillingness or inability to discuss events.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is a risk factor for adolescent suicide?
questions.rationale: Risk factors include depression, a family history of mental disorders (especially depression and suicide), past attempts, family violence, substance use, poor school performance, and hopelessness.
explanations: Poor, not good, performance is a risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q872 (PDF p. 1109)
questions.quote: a family history of mental health disorders, especially depression and suicide

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which intervention is part of suicide precautions for an acutely suicidal client?
questions.rationale: Suicide precautions mean constant observation within arm's length, meal trays without glass or metal silverware, and close watch during all activities.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q875 (PDF p. 1112)
questions.quote: Suicide precautions include maintaining arm’s length distance with the client at all times; ensuring that meal trays contain no glass or metal silverware

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: In which situation is seclusion CONTRAINDICATED?
options: A client who asks to be alone
A client who is very agitated
A client after a severe drug overdose
questions.rationale: Seclusion is contraindicated in unstable medical or mental conditions, delirium or dementia, severe suicidal tendencies, and severe drug reactions or overdoses that need close monitoring.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q877 (PDF p. 1115)
questions.quote: severe drug reactions or overdoses or the need for close monitoring

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An 8-year-old who was sexually abused is withdrawn and frightened. What is the BEST plan for the first encounter?
options: Do a full exam right away
Spend time with her and move slowly
Ask her to describe the abuse
Leave her alone until she talks
questions.rationale: Child victims fear the abuse could happen again. The nurse shows a willingness to spend time and moves slowly before any activity that may feel threatening.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q883 (PDF p. 1123)
questions.quote: it is best to convey a willingness to spend time and move slowly to initiate activities that may be perceived as threatening.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Two months after a sexual assault, a survivor says it feels 'like it happened yesterday.' Which response is BEST?
options: 'You should be moving on by now.'
'Tell me more about how you're feeling.'
questions.rationale: An open, unhurried, nonjudgmental invitation lets her express her feelings fully. Correcting her blocks communication, and the other replies are nontherapeutic.
explanations: Shifts the problem-solving burden to her.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q884 (PDF p. 1125)
questions.quote: Clients need to be reassured that their feelings are normal and that they may freely express their concerns in a safe care environment.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give staff caring for a client with paranoid personality disorder?
options: Have him sign a release form
Avoid laughing or whispering near him
questions.rationale: A paranoid client is distrustful and suspicious, and laughing or whispering nearby feeds the paranoia. The other options demand too much trust too soon.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q885 (PDF p. 1126)
questions.quote: Laughing or whispering in front of the client would increase the client’s paranoia.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A newly admitted client says, 'You won't have to worry about me much longer.' How should the nurse interpret this?
questions.rationale: This is a direct comment about not being around, which expresses suicidal intent. All suicidal statements are taken seriously.
explanations: Correct: a covert statement of suicide.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q886 (PDF p. 1128)
questions.quote: the statement that he or she will not be around is a direct comment about the act of suicide.
